Only that item's recipe step talks to it, and it holds that item's agent conversation. Who could read it again: only a retry of the same item from the recipe step. The retry route restarts the same Workflow instance, so the step reaches the same object and the conversation continues (decision 13). A later item of the same domain gets its own object. So, per item outcome: • ready: nothing will read the object again; it can be deleted as soon as the recipe step has saved the units. • failed: the object stays useful until someone retries the item, and that may never happen. Deleting it at once means a retry starts a fresh conversation; keeping it needs a point at which it goes, such as the Workflow instance's own retention. The options: (a) delete when the item reaches ready, keep failed ones forever; (b) delete on ready, and for failed items after a retention window; (c) delete at the end of the recipe step whatever the outcome, so a retry always starts fresh. Correction to the second spike (verified against settle.ts:74-102 through the scout): an item runs either the author (no saved recipe) or the revisor (its saved recipe failed on this page), never both. The author ran on an earlier item, in that item's object. So inside a per-item object the revisor has no author conversation to fork. The spike forked within one object, which only matches nagara if the agent object is per domain instead of per item. That is Q22.
